newsitem.title: USA: Charles Schwab rebounds from slow August.
newsitem.headline: Charles Schwab rebounds from slow August.

text.p: Charles Schwab Corp said Friday it was able to rebound from a trading downturn in August, bolstered by an improvement in September trading and strong growth in non-trading revenues.

In the end, the company posted a 12 percent overall increase in revenues for the third quarter ended September 30 despite a drop of more than 25 percent in its customers' daily average trading volume.
The customers' daily average trading volume, excluding mutual funds, stood at 52,300 shares in July, but then dropped to 38,000 in August, the company said.
It improved in September with daily average trading volume, excluding the mutual funds, at 45,700 shares, the company said.
When mutual funds are included, customers' daily average trading volume was 81,000 shares in July, 62,000 in August and 73,000 in September, the company said.
Charles Schwab posted $18.7 million in commissions, clearance and floor brokerage for the quarter, compared with $22.8 million the same period in the prior year.
Revenues for the quarter were $430 million, compared with $385.5 million for the same period in 1995.

"While revenue growth for the quarter fell short of our long-term threshold of 20 percent annual growth, year-to-date growth in revenues and earnings per share exceeds 30 percent," Chairman Charles Schwab said in a statement.
The company posted net income of $57.1 million, or $0.32 per share, for the quarter, compared with $47.2 million, or $0.26, in the third quarter of 1995.
